s01: Daytime, wide view over the Mê Linh countryside in the Red River delta: green rice fields, a red-brown river, a Lạc Việt village of stilt houses with curved boat-shaped thatched roofs, low hills behind. In the foreground two young Vietnamese women, the Trưng sisters, stand side by side on a small rise looking out over the land, seen from behind and slightly to the side, in deep yellow and dark red tunics, hair in high buns under dark turbans.
s02: Medium shot, daytime, inside the courtyard of a Lạc Việt chieftain's stilt house. The Trưng sisters stand side by side facing the viewer, calm and determined: the elder Trưng Trắc slightly taller on the left in a deep yellow tunic, the younger Trưng Nhị on the right in dark red, both with high buns under dark turbans and wide bronze bangles. Behind them, seated on a woven mat, their father the Lạc lord, an older Vietnamese man with a grey bun and a bronze dagger at his waist. A large bronze drum stands beside him.
s03: Daytime, a Lạc Việt village under Han rule. Han soldiers in lamellar armour with long halberds stand guard at the village edge while Vietnamese villagers in dark wrap skirts carry heavy baskets of rice and bundles toward a Han tax post: a wooden building with a tiled roof and a plain red banner with no writing. A Han official in a dark robe and black cap counts at a low table. Villagers look tired and downcast. No violence.
s04: Inside a Han governor's hall, daytime: wooden pillars, a tiled roof, plain red hangings with no writing. Governor Tô Định, a stout Han Chinese man with a thin moustache in a long black robe with wide sleeves and a black official's cap, sits on a raised wooden dais behind a low table, looking arrogant. Two Han guards in lamellar armour with halberds stand at either side. A Vietnamese servant kneels on the floor below, head bowed.
s05: Daytime at the mouth of the Hát Môn river: wide water, green banks, a few dugout boats. The Trưng sisters stand on a low earth platform at the water's edge with arms raised, swearing an oath. Before them hundreds of Lạc Việt fighters with bronze spears, axes and round woven shields raise their weapons. A large bronze drum is being struck. Plain yellow banners with no writing flutter on bamboo poles. Camera slightly elevated behind and to the side of the crowd.
s06: Daytime, a long column of Lạc Việt fighters marches across the rice fields toward a Han walled town on the horizon: rammed-earth walls, a wooden gate tower, tiled roofs. At the head of the column the Trưng sisters ride two grey war elephants with woven saddle platforms. Fighters carry bronze spears, crossbows and plain yellow banners. Dust rises from the march.
s07: Daytime at the open gate of a Han walled town. Governor Tô Định in his black robe, his official's cap falling off, flees on horseback out of the rear gate with a few frightened Han guards running behind. Behind him, small in the distance, Lạc Việt fighters with yellow banners pour over the front wall. Slightly comic panic, no blood.
s08: High wide view of the Red River delta seen from a hill, daytime. Across the land many small Han walled towns are spread out, and on the gate tower of every town a plain yellow banner now flies in place of the red one. Lạc Việt fighters wave from the walls of the nearest town. Rivers, rice fields, low hills fill the frame. The horizon sits high.
s09: Daytime, a ceremony at Mê Linh. Trưng Trắc sits on a raised wooden throne platform under a curved boat-shaped thatched roof, wearing a deep yellow robe and a bronze crown-like headband, a bronze spear upright at her side. Trưng Nhị stands beside her in dark red. Below, a crowd of Lạc Việt people and fighters bow low with hands pressed together. Two large bronze drums flank the platform. Plain yellow banners with no writing.
s10: Inside the Han imperial court, daytime: red lacquered pillars, black and red hangings with no writing. Han officials in long black robes and black caps kneel in rows, one of them holding up a bamboo-slip report. At the far end on a raised dais the Han emperor in a black robe and a flat crown with hanging bead strings looks angry. Composition symmetrical, everything clearly Han Chinese.
s11: Daytime at a Han river harbour. A large Han army prepares to march south: rows of soldiers in lamellar armour with halberds and crossbows, several war junks with square sails, supply carts. At the front, general Mã Viện, an older Han Chinese man with a grey beard in heavy lamellar armour and a helmet, sits on a horse pointing south. Plain red and black banners with no writing.
s12: Battle at Lãng Bạc, daytime, wide view across marshy ground beside a lake. On the left the Lạc Việt army with yellow banners, bronze spears and crossbows, the Trưng sisters on war elephants among them; on the right the Han army in lamellar armour with red banners and halberds. The two lines clash in the middle. Arrows in the air drawn as thin lines. No blood, no wounds.
s13: Late afternoon at Cấm Khê, a narrow valley between green hills. The Lạc Việt fighters are retreating up the valley, tired, some helping wounded comrades walk, banners lowered. The Trưng sisters, on foot now, look back over their shoulders at the Han army advancing in the distance with red banners. Muted warm light, sombre mood, no blood.
s14: Dusk on the bank of the Hát river, calm and sorrowful. The Trưng sisters stand hand in hand at the edge of the water with their backs to the viewer, looking out over the wide river toward the setting sun, their yellow and red tunics moving in the wind. The water is calm with soft golden reflections. No one else in the frame. Respectful, quiet, nothing violent.
s15: Inside a Han scholar's study, daytime, lit by a window. An old Han Chinese historian in a dark robe and black cap kneels at a low desk writing on a long bamboo-slip scroll with a brush; more bound bamboo-slip scrolls lie stacked on shelves. The writing on the slips is drawn only as abstract short black dashes, never readable characters.
s16: Daytime at Mê Linh, peaceful. A small Lạc Việt market and village life under the Trưng sisters' rule: people trading rice, fish and bronze goods, children playing, farmers in the fields, a bronze drum in the village square. In the background on a rise, the curved roof of Trưng Trắc's hall with a plain yellow banner. Warm, calm, prosperous.
s17: EXCEPTION: this single scene is set in the PRESENT DAY, so modern objects ARE allowed here. Present-day Vietnam, daytime, a tree-lined street in Hanoi: old French-style yellow buildings, motorbikes, people walking, flowering trees. At the end of the street a modern temple gate. A big street sign on a pole is drawn as a blank blue plate with NO letters on it. A group of Vietnamese schoolchildren in white shirts and red scarves walk past. Same flat cartoon style, bright and hopeful.
